title: Antarctica & Greenland Polar Ice Mass Loss (2002–2025)
source: NASA GRACE & GRACE-FO Satellite Gravimetry & ICESat-2
coords: LAT: 75.00° S | LON: 105.00° W (AMUNDSEN SEA / THWAITES SECTOR)
satellite: GRACE-FO Twin Satellites / ICESat-2 Laser Altimeter

records.explanation: 2002 GRACE Launch Baseline (0 Gt): Calm, low-volume baseline cryo-tone.
2004 (-240 Gt): Early gravimetric detection of Jakobshavn & Pine Island thinning.
2005 (-410 Gt lost): Initial ice shelf basal melt raises tension pitch.
2007 Arctic Summer Minimum: Surface meltwater lakes accelerate glacier slip.
2008 (-890 Gt lost): Melt rate accelerates to 148 Gt/yr; volume & pitch climb.
2010 (-1,190 Gt): Cumulative polar mass loss crosses 1 trillion metric tonnes.
2012 Extreme Melt Year (-1,540 Gt): 97% Greenland surface melt triggers high-delta alarm!
2014 (-1,820 Gt): Warm circumpolar deep water erodes West Antarctic grounding lines.
2016 (-2,110 Gt): Over 2 trillion tonnes of polar ice lost. High-pitch warning synth.
2018 GRACE-FO & ICESat-2 Launch: Laser altimetry maps steepening glacier calving fronts.
2019 Atmospheric Blocking Event: Extreme Greenland mass balance deficit.
2020 GRACE-FO Record (-2,680 Gt): Rapid Thwaites & Pine Island ice shelf retreat.
2022 Late-Season Heatwave (-2,940 Gt): High-elevation melt events recorded.
2024 (-3,150 Gt): Over 3.1 trillion tonnes lost since 2002 baseline.
2025 Cumulative Loss (-3,340 Gt): Maximum anomaly! High-pitch siren & bass sub-drop.
